worker.label: Worker
worker.title: What this could mean for my retirement
worker.lede: Pension funds have long held private markets. Most 401(k)s, where workers now do most of their saving, hold almost none.
worker.concernsLede: Short answers, and what to keep in mind.

employer.label: Employer
employer.title: What this means for our plan
employer.lede: Pension plans have long held private markets. Most 401(k) menus hold almost none, and adding them is a fiduciary decision.
employer.concernsTitle: What a plan committee will weigh
employer.concernsLede: Short answers, and what to keep in mind.

points.text: Workers wouldn't buy a private fund themselves.

source.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)

points.text: The private slice sits inside an option already on the menu: a target date fund, a managed account or a professionally managed portfolio, often set up as a collective investment trust.

source.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)

points.text: Perpetual funds make this workable: they invest new money right away and allow periodic rebalancing. Older drawdown funds didn't.

source.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)

objections.title: Fees
objections.question: Private funds cost more. Does the extra return survive?

concern.text: Each fund on this map charges a yearly management fee plus a share of returns above a hurdle. Any extra return has to clear both first.

sources.name: BREIT Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026
sources.page: Note 10: Related Party and Other Transactions

sources.name: BX Infra Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026
BCRED Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026
sources.page: Note 3: Fees, Expenses, Agreements and Related Party Transactions

response.text: The paper's worker ends about $500k ahead at 65. The Labor Department's proposal asks employers to judge performance after fees, not fees alone.

sources.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)
Gibson Dunn, DOL Proposes Safe Harbor for Selection of Designated Investment Alternatives in 401(k) Plans (Apr 2026)

objections.watch: The private slice's return after all fees, next to a public benchmark. The paper's indices carry no fund fees.

objections.title: Liquidity
objections.question: What happens when everyone wants out at once?

concern.text: Private funds can limit withdrawals. In December 2022, BREIT filled 4% of the repurchases investors asked for.

response.text: A saver wouldn't own the private fund directly. The target date fund's manager handles withdrawals, and perpetual funds allow periodic rebalancing.

sources.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)

objections.watch: How far above target the private slice can drift, and the private funds' own repurchase limits.

objections.title: Valuation
objections.question: A 401(k) prices daily. Private assets don't.

concern.text: Private assets are valued by appraisal, which moves gradually. Ups and downs show up later and smaller than in a traded price.

sources.name: GPIF, working paper on private real estate return smoothing (2023)

response.text: The Labor Department's proposal makes valuation one of six factors an employer must weigh before adding any option.

sources.name: Gibson Dunn, DOL Proposes Safe Harbor for Selection of Designated Investment Alternatives in 401(k) Plans (Apr 2026)

objections.watch: How often the private slice is valued, and by whom.

link.label: Why are the values so smooth?

objections.title: Lawsuits
objections.question: Could the employer be sued for adding it?

concern.text: In Anderson v. Intel, a worker says putting retirement money into hedge funds and private equity through custom target date funds was imprudent. The Supreme Court heard it on Oct 6, 2026.

sources.name: Ropes & Gray, Supreme Court Chooses to Hear Intel (Jan 2026)
Supreme Court of the United States, argument audio, No. 25-498

response.text: Lower courts dismissed that case, judging the process rather than the result. The Labor Department's proposed safe harbor would presume a careful process prudent.

sources.name: Ropes & Gray, Supreme Court Chooses to Hear Intel (Jan 2026)
Gibson Dunn, DOL Proposes Safe Harbor for Selection of Designated Investment Alternatives in 401(k) Plans (Apr 2026)

objections.watch: The Supreme Court's decision, and whether the Labor Department finalizes its rule.

objections.title: Complexity
objections.question: Can workers and employers understand what they own?

concern.text: Layered fees, appraised values and withdrawal limits are harder to follow. Complexity is one of the six factors in the Labor Department's proposal.

sources.name: Gibson Dunn, DOL Proposes Safe Harbor for Selection of Designated Investment Alternatives in 401(k) Plans (Apr 2026)

response.text: Workers wouldn't pick private funds. A professional manager would hold the slice inside an option already on the menu, such as a target date fund.

sources.name: Blackstone, Expanding Retirement Investors' Access to Private Markets (2026)

objections.watch: Whether the plan explains the private slice in plain language.
